strings.m01.title: Welcome and your account
strings.m01.s1: I have given Paint Group my ABN, my GST status and my bank details.
strings.m01.s2: I will upload my public liability insurance before my first job. Job offers start when it is in.
strings.m01.s3: If I bring more than one worker, I need WorkCover.
strings.m01.s4: I understand the induction day is unpaid.
strings.m01.s5: I understand that 12 Demo Street is a practice job and nothing in it is real.
strings.m01.tick: I have set up my account.
strings.m02.title: How a Paint Group job runs
strings.m02.s1: A job has nine steps: Offer, Accept, Pre-start, Work days, Pre-defect, Walk-through, Sign-off, Invoice, Paid.
strings.m02.s2: Paint Group quotes the job, books it, orders the materials, talks to the customer and pays me.
strings.m02.s3: I accept the job, paint it, update the app, check my own work and run the walk-through.
strings.m02.s4: The walk-through is booked for the last day when I accept. If my finish date changes, I log it in the app the day I know.
strings.m02.tick: I know the nine steps of a job.
strings.m02.w1: My contractor accepts the job, raises variations and invoices. I paint, take photos and tick my surfaces.
strings.m03.title: In a customer's home
strings.m03.s1: I am a guest in the customer's home. I am polite, and I ask before I use anything.
strings.m03.s2: Shoes off until the floors are covered. I cover every floor fully and tape hard-floor protection at the edges.
strings.m03.s3: Before I start I ask: where to park, where to leave materials, and whether I may use the toilet, power and water.
strings.m03.s4: No smoking, drugs or alcohol. No eating inside an occupied home. Music only if the customer is happy, and I ask first.
strings.m03.s5: I keep pets and children away from wet paint and ladders. I do not move valuables. I ask the customer to.
strings.m03.s6: At the end of every day: materials packed and covered in the agreed place, rubbish in one place, wet-paint signs up, doors and windows I opened locked, keys and alarm as agreed.
strings.m03.s7: I never wash brushes in the customer's sink or garden. I never take photos of the home except the work. I never post anything online.
strings.m03.s8: I never bring anyone who is not on my crew.
strings.m03.s9: I check the colour schedule before I open a tin.
strings.m03.s10: If I cannot come or will be late, I tell Paint Group the day before, or before 7:30 am on the day. I never leave the customer waiting with no message.
strings.m03.tick: I will follow the site rules in every home.
strings.m04.title: Materials and equipment
strings.m04.s1: Paint Group supplies the paint and everything I use up: filler, caulk, tape, drop sheets, floor protection, sandpaper, rollers and brushes.
strings.m04.s2: I bring my tools: ladders, spray equipment, pots, trays, poles, sanding equipment and power tools.
strings.m04.s3: Materials are delivered to site where possible, otherwise ordered to the nearest paint shop. The work order shows which.
strings.m04.s4: If I am short of something, I request more in the app or I call. I never leave a job waiting.
strings.m04.s5: I do not arrange colour matches myself. Paint Group sets them up first.
strings.m04.s6: Loan gear goes back in the same condition I got it.
strings.m04.tick: I know what we supply and what I bring.
strings.m04.w1: If something is running out, I tell my contractor straight away.
strings.m05.title: Finish standards
strings.m05.s1: The three levels — what Level 2, 3 and 4 mean, and the look test at 3 m, 1.5 m and 0.5 m.
strings.m05.s2: Rules for every job — drips, paint in the wrong place, hardware, protect first, full cover, clean finish, clean site.
strings.m05.s3: Your time — what standard preparation includes, what earns extra time (bogging, stain blocking, additional coats), and the variation steps.
strings.m05.s4: Interior surfaces — the list for walls, ceilings, cornices, skirting boards, architraves, window frames and doors at each level.
strings.m05.s5: Exterior surfaces — the list for weatherboards, brick, render, picket fences, windows, doors, fascias, eaves, strapping and fretwork at each level.
strings.m05.s6: The defect rule — find and fix your own defects before the customer sees them; the tape check on jobs of 16 hours or more.
strings.m05.tick: The six standards ticks, one per section.
strings.m06.title: Quality checks and your status light
strings.m06.s1: A clean job is: the app kept up to date from the reminder prompts, every quality check passed first time, and no call back in the 7 days after sign-off.
strings.m06.s2: When a reminder prompt arrives, I update the job that day.
strings.m06.s3: I start on New. Four clean jobs in a row take me to Green. After that, my last ten jobs decide my colour.
strings.m06.s4: Green: priority on new jobs, paid within 3 business days of sign-off, bonus eligible. Yellow: normal. Orange: offers after Green and Yellow, a check on every job, a call from my Project Coordinator. Red: no more job offers. We meet to go through the level of finish expected on my current job.
strings.m06.s5: Four clean jobs in a row take me back to Green from any colour.
strings.m06.s6: The status light is a reward system. It never takes money off my payment.
strings.m06.tick: I understand how my status works and what Red means.
strings.m06.w1: My work counts toward my contractor's status light.
strings.m07.title: Talking to the customer
strings.m07.s1: I say hello on day one and explain today's work. I answer simple questions about today's work. I keep the site clean and I update the app.
strings.m07.s2: I pass everything else to Paint Group: price, scope, the level of finish, variations, colour changes, dates, complaints, call backs and invoices.
strings.m07.s3: If I will be late or cannot come, I tell Paint Group the day before, or before 7:30 am on the day.
strings.m07.s4: If my finish date changes, I log it in the app the day I know.
strings.m07.s5: If a customer is unhappy: I stay calm, I listen, and we look at the area together from the right distance. I fix it now if it is our standard and quick. Anything else: no promises, photos, a note in the app, and I call Paint Group the same day.
strings.m07.s6: I never agree a price, a big extra or a change of scope on site. I say: "Good question. I will ask Paint Group to call you today."
strings.m07.tick: I know what I say to the customer and what Paint Group says.
strings.m08.title: Variations
strings.m08.s1: The work order is the scope. Anything not itemised in it can be a variation.
strings.m08.s2: Small items missed from the scope are part of the job. What is small depends on the job: on a long job a few metres of fascia or one door in fifty is expected; on a short job a missed window frame is a variation. A whole room, a ceiling not in the scope or a second colour is always a variation.
strings.m08.s3: I log a variation the moment I see it, with photos and hours. Not at the end of the job.
strings.m08.s4: I never start the extra work before the customer has approved it.
strings.m08.s5: Standard preparation, paint applied too thin and something I missed in my own work are never variations.
strings.m08.s6: Not sure? I ask before I start.
strings.m08.tick: I know what a variation is and how to log one.
strings.m08.w1: If I see something missing from the scope, or something extra, I tell my contractor straight away. I never agree an extra with the customer.
strings.m09.title: Pre-defect, walk-through and call backs
strings.m09.s1: I find and fix my own defects before the customer sees them.
strings.m09.s2: On jobs of 16 hours or more I tape every defect, fix it, and take the tape off. No tape left means ready. On smaller jobs I still check every surface.
strings.m09.s3: Before the walk-through: site clean, rubbish gone, floors uncovered, hardware back, windows and doors open and close, final photos in the app.
strings.m09.s4: I lead the walk-through from the front door, one room at a time. Small things I fix there and then. Anything bigger: a note in the app, no promises, and Paint Group calls the customer.
strings.m09.s5: A call back is a return visit on another day to fix workmanship. It counts for 7 days after sign-off. Fixed and signed the same day is not a call back.
strings.m09.tick: I check my own work before every walk-through.
strings.m10.title: The app day to day
strings.m10.s1: I accept or decline a job offer within 24 hours. Accepting means the dates are mine.
strings.m10.s2: My workers each have a login and do the worker induction before I share a job with them. Invoices, variations and messages stay with me.
strings.m10.s3: I take a before photo of each area before I touch it.
strings.m10.s4: I tick each surface as it moves from To do to Prepped to Painted, on the day.
strings.m10.s5: I update the app on my first day, then every 2 to 3 days, and on the day a reminder prompt arrives.
strings.m10.s6: If I have a question, I ask in the app. If I am not working on a booked day, I tell Paint Group in the morning.
strings.m10.tick: I know how to run a job in the app.
strings.m10.w1: I tick my own work under my own name.
strings.m11.title: Money
strings.m11.s1: My price is on the offer: hours times the rate, plus approved variations. I never haggle with Paint Group or with the customer.
strings.m11.s2: After sign-off I create the invoice in the app, check it and submit it.
strings.m11.s3: I am paid on normal terms after sign-off. Green painters are paid within 3 business days. A missing sign-off or missing before photos delays payment.
strings.m11.s4: I claim expenses with a receipt photo, the amount, the category and the job. Over $100, I ask first.
strings.m11.tick: I know how to invoice and claim expenses.
strings.m12.title: Calendar
strings.m12.s1: I keep my calendar true. I block out days I cannot work before Paint Group books me.
strings.m12.s2: Blocking a day does not change a job already booked on it. For that, I tell Paint Group straight away.
strings.m12.s3: My Paint Group jobs can show in my own Google Calendar. Changing them there does not change the job.
strings.m12.tick: My calendar is up to date and linked.
strings.m13.title: Safety basics
strings.m13.s1: I use ladders footed, on a level base, with three points of contact. For big ladders and scaffold I ask Paint Group.
strings.m13.s2: If I think I have found lead paint or asbestos, I stop, I do not sand or scrape, and I call Paint Group.
strings.m13.s3: I sand with extraction or wet, I ventilate, and I put up wet-paint signs where people walk.
strings.m13.s4: I am responsible for everyone I bring. They work to the same rules. Every worker has a white card.
strings.m13.s5: If something at the home is unsafe, I stop and call Paint Group before I continue.
strings.m13.tick: I will work safely and so will my crew.
strings.m00.title: What is changing
strings.m00.s1: The finish standards, the site rules and who says what to the customer are written down in the app. I read them and tick them.
strings.m00.s2: A call back is a return visit on another day to fix workmanship. It counts for 7 days after sign-off.
strings.m00.s3: My status light decides how I am offered work. Four clean jobs in a row take me to Green. Red means no more offers until we have met.
strings.m00.s4: Small things missed from the scope are part of the job. Anything bigger is a variation, logged the moment I see it.
strings.standards.levels.intro: The level on your work order tells you how much preparation to do and how fine the finish must be. Level 2 repairs what is broken. Level 3 fixes what a customer can see from 1.5 m. Level 4 fixes what a customer can see up close.
strings.standards.levels.items.2.name: Clean, tidy repaint
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.1.label: Filling
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.1.text: All holes, nail holes and open cracks. Small marks in the old surface can stay.
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.2.label: Sanding
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.2.text: Light sand. Remove loose paint and dust.
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.3.label: Gaps (caulking)
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.4.label: Old problems (old runs, old paint on glass, old brush marks)
strings.standards.levels.items.2.summary.5.label: Look test
strings.standards.levels.items.3.name: Our standard finish
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.1.label: Filling
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.1.text: Every mark you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.2.label: Sanding
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.3.label: Gaps (caulking)
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.4.label: Old problems (old runs, old paint on glass, old brush marks)
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.4.text: Fix what you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.levels.items.3.summary.5.label: Look test
strings.standards.levels.items.4.name: Premium finish
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.1.label: Filling
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.1.text: Every mark you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.2.label: Sanding
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.2.text: Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats.
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.3.label: Gaps (caulking)
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.4.label: Old problems (old runs, old paint on glass, old brush marks)
strings.standards.levels.items.4.summary.5.label: Look test
strings.standards.levels.look_test_steps.1: First, do everything in the list for the surface. The list is the rule.
strings.standards.levels.look_test_steps.2: Then stand back at the distance for the level on your work order.
strings.standards.levels.look_test_steps.3: Look straight at the surface in normal light: daylight, or the room lights on. Do not use a torch.
strings.standards.levels.look_test_steps.4: If you can see a problem from that distance, fix it.
strings.standards.levels.look_test_high_areas: For high areas (ceilings, cornices, eaves, fascias, second storey), do the look test from the floor or the ground.
strings.standards.levels.closing: If your work order does not show a level, ask us before you start.
strings.standards.rules.intro: These rules are the same at Level 2, Level 3 and Level 4. Every job must finish clean, with no drips and no paint on anything that should not be painted.
strings.standards.rules.items.1.meaning: No drips, runs or sags on any painted surface.
strings.standards.rules.items.2.rule: No paint where it should not be
strings.standards.rules.items.2.meaning: No paint on floors, carpet, tiles, benchtops, cupboards, furniture, switches, power points, lights, paths, driveways, decks, roofs, plants or cars.
strings.standards.rules.items.3.meaning: No paint on handles, hinges, locks, latches, window winders or door stops. Remove the hardware or mask it.
strings.standards.rules.items.4.meaning: Cover floors and furniture with drop sheets and plastic before you start.
strings.standards.rules.items.5.meaning: No missed spots, no thin patches and no old colour showing through.
strings.standards.rules.items.6.meaning: No dust, hair, grit or brush hairs stuck in the paint.
strings.standards.rules.items.7.meaning: Remove job rubbish every day. Leave your materials tidy before you go.
strings.standards.rules.items.8.meaning: Remove all tape, plastic, drop sheets, empty tins and rubbish. Clean up sanding dust. Put back any hardware or cover plates you removed.
strings.standards.rules.closing: If you spill or drip paint, clean it straight away. If it will not come off, tell us the same day.
strings.standards.time.intro: The time on your work order for each surface already includes all standard preparation for that level. You are not paid extra for standard preparation.
strings.standards.time.standard_preparation.inte: Fill holes, nail holes, cracks and dents to the level on your work order.
Fill gaps with gap filler to the level on your work order.
Sand to the level on your work order.
Sand and clean glossy surfaces so new paint will stick.
Prime all filler and bare patches.
strings.standards.time.standard_preparation.exte: Wash or clean the surface. Paint only clean, dry surfaces.
Scrape and sand loose and peeling paint.
Fill holes and cracks in timber to the level on your work order.
Fill gaps with exterior gap filler to the level on your work order.
Sand to the level on your work order.
Prime all bare timber and bare patches.
Protect paths, plants and anything not being painted.
strings.standards.time.extra_time_intro: Some areas need more than standard preparation. When we see this at the quote, we add extra time to your work order for it.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.1.name: Bogging
strings.standards.time.extra_time.1.meaning: Heavy repairs with two-part filler (builder's bog). Normal filler cannot do this job.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.1.examples: Rotten timber on sills, fascias and weatherboards. Deep holes. Broken corners and edges.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.2.name: Stain blocking
strings.standards.time.extra_time.2.meaning: Sealing a stain with stain-block primer, so it does not come through the new paint.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.2.examples: Water stains on ceilings. Smoke and nicotine. Timber stain (tannin) bleeding through. Mould marks after cleaning. Pen and marker.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.3.name: Additional coats
strings.standards.time.extra_time.3.meaning: More coats than normal, so the new colour covers fully.
strings.standards.time.extra_time.3.examples: A big colour change, dark to light or light to dark. Bare or new surfaces that need a primer or undercoat. Colours that cover poorly, such as strong yellows and reds.
strings.standards.time.variation_intro: If you find an area that needs extra time and it is not on your work order, you can charge a variation.
strings.standards.time.variation_steps.1: Stop before you do the extra work.
strings.standards.time.variation_steps.2: Take clear photos of the problem.
strings.standards.time.variation_steps.3: Raise a variation in your portal. Say what the problem is and how many extra hours it needs.
strings.standards.time.variation_steps.4: Wait for us to approve it. The customer must agree to the extra cost first.
strings.standards.time.variation_steps.5: Do the work when the variation is approved.
strings.standards.time.closing: Standard preparation is never a variation. Paint applied too thin is not a reason for an additional coat: apply every coat at the thickness on the tin.
strings.standards.interior.intro: Find the surface, then read the column for the level on your work order. The rules for every job always apply as well.
strings.standards.exterior.intro: Find the surface, then read the column for the level on your work order. These five rules apply to every exterior surface, at every level.
strings.standards.exterior.rules.1: Paint only clean, dry, solid surfaces.
strings.standards.exterior.rules.2: Scrape off all loose and flaking paint. Prime all bare timber and bare patches before the top coats.
strings.standards.exterior.rules.3: No paint on paths, driveways, decks, roofs, gutters, plants, cars or the neighbour's property, unless it is on your work order.
strings.standards.exterior.rules.4: Rotten timber needs bogging. Check your work order for bogging time. If there is none, raise a variation.
strings.standards.exterior.rules.5: Old homes can have asbestos sheet or lead paint. If you think you have found either, stop. Do not sand or scrape. Call us.
strings.standards.defect.intro: You find and fix your own defects before the customer sees them. You mark every defect with tape before the walk-through, and you fix every taped defect before the final walk-through.
strings.standards.defect.small_job_note: On jobs under 16 hours, the tape step is not required. You still check your own work and fix every defect before the walk-through.
strings.standards.defect.steps.1: Finish all painting and clean the site.
strings.standards.defect.steps.2: Walk through every room, or every side of the house, on your own.
strings.standards.defect.steps.3: Do the look test on every surface, at the distance for the level on your work order.
strings.standards.defect.steps.4: Put a small piece of painter's tape next to every defect you find.
strings.standards.defect.steps.5: Fix every taped defect. Take the tape off as you fix each one.
strings.standards.defect.steps.6: Check that all tape is gone. The job is now ready for the final walk-through.
strings.standards.defect.why.1: Fewer defects are found at the final walk-through.
strings.standards.defect.why.2: The customer sees that we are one step ahead.
strings.standards.defect.why.3: You finish the job in one visit and you do not have to come back.
strings.standards.defect.defects.1.examples: Runs, drips, sags, missed spots, thin patches, old colour showing through, roller lines, patchy areas.
strings.standards.defect.defects.2.defect: Preparation not done to the level
strings.standards.defect.defects.2.examples: Holes, cracks or gaps not filled. Filler not sanded flat. Rough areas not sanded.
strings.standards.defect.defects.3.examples: Wavy or untidy lines between colours, at ceilings, trim and glass.
strings.standards.defect.defects.4.examples: Paint on glass, hardware, floors, switches, power points, paths or furniture.
strings.standards.defect.defects.5.examples: Dust, hair, grit or brush hairs stuck in the paint.
strings.standards.defect.defects.6.examples: Windows or doors stuck with paint. Hardware or cover plates not put back.
strings.standards.defect.closing: If the customer or our team finds a defect at the final walk-through, you fix it before the job is signed off.
strings.standards.checklist.intro: Check these eight things before you tell us the job is finished.
strings.standards.checklist.items.1: Every surface on the work order is painted, with the number of coats on the work order.
strings.standards.checklist.items.2: Preparation on every surface matches the level on the work order.
strings.standards.checklist.items.3: No drips, runs, missed spots or patchy areas.
strings.standards.checklist.items.4: No paint on glass, hardware, floors, switches, paths or anything not being painted.
strings.standards.checklist.items.5: All windows and doors open and close.
strings.standards.checklist.items.6: All hardware and cover plates are back in place.
strings.standards.checklist.items.7: You have found and fixed your own defects. If you used tape, all tape is removed.
strings.standards.checklist.items.8: The site is clean: no rubbish, no tape, no plastic, no dust.
strings.standards.words.items.1.meaning: The standard of preparation and finish for the job: 2, 3 or 4. It is on your work order.
strings.standards.words.items.2.meaning: Stand back at the distance for the level. If you can see a problem, fix it.
strings.standards.words.items.3.meaning: Put filler in holes, dents and cracks, then sand it flat.
strings.standards.words.items.4.meaning: Flexible filler for gaps and joins between two surfaces.
strings.standards.words.items.5.meaning: Strong two-part filler for heavy repairs, such as rotten timber.
strings.standards.words.items.6.meaning: The corner join where two pieces of trim meet at an angle.
strings.standards.words.items.7.meaning: A first coat on bare timber, bare patches or filler, so the top coats stick and cover evenly.
strings.standards.words.items.8.meaning: A special primer that stops a stain coming through new paint.
strings.standards.words.items.9.meaning: Sand the edge of old paint or filler until you cannot feel a step. Also called feathering.
strings.standards.words.items.10.meaning: Handles, locks, latches, hinges, winders and door stops.
strings.standards.words.items.11.meaning: Anything that does not meet the standard for the level.
strings.standards.words.items.12.meaning: Extra paid work that is not on your work order. It must be approved before you do it.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.name: Walls
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.every_level: Full, even cover. No patchy areas, no roller lines and no missed spots. Prime all filler and bare patches before the top coats, so repairs do not show through. No paint on switches or power points.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.1.label: Fill
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.1.l2: All holes, nail and screw holes, open cracks and deep dents. Small dents and light scratches can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.1.l3: Every hole, dent, crack and mark you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.1.l4: Every hole, dent, crack and mark you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.2.label: Sand
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.2.l2: Sand filler flat. Remove loose paint, lumps and dust.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.2.l3: Sand filler flat with soft edges, so the patch cannot be seen from 1.5 m. Sand the whole wall.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.2.l4: Sand the whole wall before the first coat and lightly between coats. Patches cannot be seen from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.3.label: Old surface
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.3.l2: Old roller texture, old patches and old drips can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.3.l3: Remove old drips and lumps you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.3.l4: Remove all old drips, lumps and rough patches.
strings.standards.surfaces.walls.checks.4.label: Lines
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.name: Ceilings
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.every_level: Even, flat finish. No roller lines, no patchy areas and no missed spots. No ceiling paint on walls, lights, fans, vents or smoke alarms. Do the look test from the floor.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.1.l2: Holes and open cracks. Fine cracks (thinner than 1 mm) can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.1.l3: Every hole, crack and dent you can see from the floor.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.1.l4: Every hole, crack and dent. Also check by looking across the ceiling toward the window.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.2.l2: Scrape loose and flaking paint. Sand filler flat.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.2.l3: Sand filler flat with soft edges. Sand the edges of scraped paint smooth. Sand the whole ceiling.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.2.l4: Sand the whole ceiling before the first coat and lightly between coats. No old patch or paint edge showing.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.3.l2: Tell us about any water stain. Stain blocking is extra time.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.3.l3: Tell us about any water stain. Stain blocking is extra time.
strings.standards.surfaces.ceilings.checks.3.l4: Tell us about any water stain. Stain blocking is extra time.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.name: Cornices
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.every_level: Full cover, including inside the pattern on decorative cornices. No thick paint filling the pattern. Straight lines where the cornice meets a different colour.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.note: Broken or missing pieces of cornice are a repair. Tell us before you start.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.1.l2: Open gaps and cracks between cornice and wall, and between cornice and ceiling.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.1.l3: Also the corner joins (mitres) and joins along the length.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.1.l4: Every gap and join filled and smooth. No join can be seen from the floor.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.2.l3: Every chip and hole you can see from the floor.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.3.l3: Sand filler smooth. Remove old drips.
strings.standards.surfaces.cornices.checks.3.l4: Sand filler and old paint edges smooth. Remove all old drips.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.name: Skirting boards
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.every_level: No paint on the floor or carpet. Clean dust and hair off the skirting and the floor edge before you paint. Straight line along the top. No runs.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.1.l2: Holes, nail holes and open cracks. Small dents and knocks can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.1.l3: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.1.l4: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.2.l2: Top edge, where the skirting meets the wall.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.2.l4: Every gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.3.l2: Light sand to remove loose paint and take the shine off.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.3.l3: Sand well until smooth to touch. Remove old runs and drips.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.3.l4: Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. No old brush marks or runs showing.
strings.standards.surfaces.skirting.checks.4.l4: Smooth and even from 0.5 m. Very light brush marks only.
strings.standards.surfaces.architraves.name: Architraves
strings.standards.surfaces.architraves.every_lev: No paint on hinges, door hardware or the floor. Straight lines where the architrave meets the wall. Door frames follow this same standard.
Holes, nail holes and open cracks. Small dents and knocks can stay.
Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 1.5 m.
Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 0.5 m.
Outside edge, where the architrave meets the wall.
Outside edge, top corners (mitres) and the join to the door or window frame.
Every gap and join, filled smooth.
Light sand to remove loose paint and take the shine off.
Sand well until smooth to touch. Remove old runs and drips.
Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. No old brush marks or runs showing.
Smooth and even from 0.5 m. Very light brush marks only.
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.name: Window frames
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.every_le: No paint on hardware: locks, latches, handles, winders, hinges, tracks, rubber seals and flyscreens. Remove the hardware or mask it. Windows must open and close after painting. Do not scratch the glass when you scrape it.
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.checks.1: Remove all paint that you put on the glass. Old paint on the glass can stay.
Remove all paint from the glass, new and old, for sharp lines.
Remove all paint from the glass. Sharp, straight lines on every pane. Leave the glass clean.
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.checks.2: Large holes, nail holes and cracks in the timber. Minor defects in the timber can stay.
Every mark you can see from 1.5 m.
Every mark you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.checks.3: Edges of the frame, where the frame meets the wall.
Edges, mitres and corners of the frame.
Every gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.windowframes.checks.4: Light sand to remove loose paint and dirt only.
Sand well for a smooth finish.
Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. Remove old runs and brush marks.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.name: Doors
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.every_level: No paint on hardware: handles, locks, latches, hinges and door stops. Remove the hardware or mask it. Paint the faces and every edge you can see. The door must open and close without sticking. No runs in panel corners or on edges.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.1.label: Fill
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.1.l2: Holes, cracks, deep dents and chipped edges. Small dents can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.1.l3: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.1.l4: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.2.label: Sand
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.2.l2: Light sand to remove loose paint and take the shine off.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.2.l3: Sand the whole door smooth. Remove old runs and drips.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.2.l4: Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. No old brush marks, runs or roller texture showing.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.3.label: Finish
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.3.l2: Even cover. No runs. Light brush or roller marks are OK.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.3.l3: Smooth, with an even shine. Brush marks all run the same way.
strings.standards.surfaces.doors.checks.3.l4: Smooth and even from 0.5 m on faces and edges.
strings.standards.surfaces.weatherboards.name: Weatherboards
strings.standards.surfaces.weatherboards.every_l: Paint the bottom edge of every board. Do not fill the gap under each board, because boards need to move. No missed spots at board ends and corners.
Scrape all loose paint. Light sand of rough edges. Edges of old paint can show.
Scrape all loose paint. Sand the edges of old paint soft, so they are hard to see from 1.5 m.
Scrape and sand every board. Old paint edges cannot be seen from 0.5 m.
Open splits and large holes. Nail heads can show.
Splits, holes and nail holes you can see from 1.5 m.
Every split, hole and nail hole you can see from 0.5 m.
Where boards meet window frames, door frames and corner boards.
Also open joins between board ends.
Every upright gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.name: Brick
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.intro: For painted brick, the three levels are almost the same. The difference is crack filling.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.every_level: Brush off dirt, cobwebs and loose paint first. Full cover inside every mortar joint. Check from the left, from the right and from below: no bare spots. Straight lines at the ground, paths and windows.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.1.label: Cracks
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.1.l2: No filling needed. Cracks can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.1.l3: Fill open cracks in mortar and bricks that you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.1.l4: Fill every crack you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.2.label: Finish
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.2.l3: Full cover. No roller lines from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.brick.checks.2.l4: Full cover. No roller lines from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.name: Render
strings.standards.surfaces.render.every_level: Even cover. No roller lines and no patchy areas. Do not paint over loose or hollow render. Tell us, because it is a repair.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.1.label: Cracks
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.1.l2: Fill open cracks. Fine cracks (thinner than 1 mm) can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.1.l3: Fill every crack you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.1.l4: Fill every crack you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.2.label: Repairs
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.2.l3: Filler flat, with texture to match. Hard to see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.render.checks.2.l4: Filler flat, with texture to match. Cannot be seen from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.name: Picket fence
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.every_level: Paint the sides on your work order. On those sides, paint every face: front, both edges and the top of each picket, plus rails and posts. No missed strips between pickets. No drips at the bottom of pickets. No paint on paths, plants or the neighbour's side.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.note: Loose, broken or rotten pickets are a repair. Tell us before you paint them.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.1.label: Scrape and sand
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.1.l3: Scrape loose paint. Sand the edges of old paint soft.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.1.l4: Scrape and sand every picket smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.2.label: Fill
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.2.l3: Holes and splits you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.picket.checks.2.l4: Every hole and split you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.name: Windows
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.every_leve: No paint on hardware: locks, latches, handles, winders, hinges, tracks, rubber seals and flyscreens. Remove the hardware or mask it. Windows must open and close after painting. Do not scratch the glass. Sills get the most weather, so prepare and prime them fully.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.note: Loose or missing putty and rotten timber need extra time. Check your work order. If no extra time is allowed, raise a variation.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.checks.1.l: Remove all paint that you put on the glass. Old paint on the glass can stay.
Remove all paint from the glass, new and old, for sharp lines.
Remove all paint from the glass. Sharp, straight lines on every pane. Leave the glass clean.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.checks.2.l: Scrape loose paint. Light sand to remove loose paint and dirt only.
Scrape loose paint. Sand well for a smooth finish.
Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. Remove old runs and brush marks.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.checks.3.l: Large holes, nail holes and cracks in the timber. Minor defects in the timber can stay.
Every mark you can see from 1.5 m.
Every mark you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.extwindows.checks.4.l: Edges of the frame, where the frame meets the wall.
Edges, mitres and corners of the frame and sill.
Every gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.name: Doors
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.every_level: No paint on hardware: handles, locks, hinges, door numbers, door bells, letter slots and rubber seals. Remove the hardware or mask it. Paint the faces and every edge you can see. The door must close and lock without sticking. No runs in panel corners or on edges.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.1.l2: Holes, cracks, deep dents and chipped edges. Small dents can stay.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.1.l3: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 1.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.1.l4: Every hole, dent and chip you can see from 0.5 m.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.2.l2: Scrape loose paint. Light sand to take the shine off.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.2.l3: Sand the whole door smooth. Remove old runs and drips.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.2.l4: Sand smooth before the first coat and between coats. No old brush marks, runs or roller texture showing.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.3.l2: Even cover. No runs. Light brush or roller marks are OK.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.3.l3: Smooth, with an even shine. Brush marks all run the same way.
strings.standards.surfaces.extdoors.checks.3.l4: Smooth and even from 0.5 m on faces and edges.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.name: Fascias
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.every_level: Paint the face and the bottom edge. No paint on gutters, roof tiles or roof sheets, unless they are on your work order. Do the look test from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.checks.1.l3: Scrape loose paint. Sand the edges of old paint soft.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.checks.1.l4: Scrape and sand smooth. No old paint edge can be seen from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.checks.2.l3: Splits, holes and nail holes you can see from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.checks.2.l4: Every split, hole and nail hole.
strings.standards.surfaces.fascias.checks.3.l4: Every gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.name: Eaves
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.every_level: Clean off cobwebs, dirt and mould before you paint. Even cover with no roller lines. No paint on walls, lights or vents, unless they are on your work order. Do the look test from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.1.label: Fill
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.1.l3: Holes and cracks you can see from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.2.label: Gaps
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.2.l3: Open gaps where the eave meets the fascia or timber trim.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.2.l4: Every gap and join, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.3.label: Lines
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.3.l3: Sharp and straight from the ground.
strings.standards.surfaces.eaves.checks.3.l4: Sharp and straight from the ground, on every edge.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.name: Strapping
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.intro: Strapping means the cover strips over the joins in sheet eaves, gables and walls.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.every_level: Paint the face and both edges of every strip. No missed lines along the edges.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.note: Loose or broken strips are a repair. Tell us before you paint them.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.checks.1.l3: Nail holes and splits you can see from 1.5 m, or from the ground for high areas.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.checks.2.l3: Open gaps between the strip and the sheet that you can see.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.checks.2.l4: Both edges of every strip, filled smooth.
strings.standards.surfaces.strapping.checks.3.la: Lines (when the strip is a different colour)
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.name: Fretwork
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.intro: Fretwork means the decorative timber on verandahs and gables.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.every_level: Paint every face and edge, including inside the cut-outs. Check from the front, from the back and from below. No runs, drips or thick paint in corners and cut-outs.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.note: Rotten or broken fretwork needs bogging or a repair. Check your work order. If no extra time is allowed, raise a variation.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.checks.1.l3: Scrape loose paint. Sand the edges of old paint soft.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.checks.1.l4: Scrape and sand smooth. The pattern stays sharp.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.checks.2.l3: Splits and holes you can see from 1.5 m, or from the ground for high areas.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.checks.3.l3: Open joins where the fretwork meets posts and beams.
strings.standards.surfaces.fretwork.checks.3.l4: Every gap and join, filled smooth.
